---
title: Ollama Embeddings
guide-section: Building a Store
bread-crumbs: false
---

[Ollama](https://ollama.com) runs chat and embedding models on your computer. You download a model with `ollama pull`, then use Ollama's API to create embeddings. With a local model, the text you embed stays on your machine, and you don't need an API key.

raghilda connects to this API through `EmbeddingOllama`. This guide shows how to set it up, choose a model, and connect to an Ollama server on your computer or another machine.

## Installation

First, download and install Ollama from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com/download). Once it's running, pull an embedding model from the command line:

```bash
ollama pull embeddinggemma-2
```

This downloads [EmbeddingGemma 2](https://ollama.com/library/embeddinggemma-2), the model `EmbeddingOllama` uses by default.

You don't need any additional Python packages. `EmbeddingOllama` uses the `openai` client library, which already comes with raghilda.

## Basic usage

Once Ollama is running and you've downloaded the model, create a provider. By default, it connects to `http://localhost:11434/v1` and uses `embeddinggemma-2:latest`:

::: {#60796f2f .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingOllama

provider = EmbeddingOllama()
```
:::


To use a different model, pass its name exactly as it appears in `ollama list`:

::: {#b47cbb2c .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
provider = EmbeddingOllama(model="mxbai-embed-large")
```
:::


Pass the provider to a store through the `embed=` argument:

::: {#3f5b2793 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingOllama

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="my_store.db",
    embed=EmbeddingOllama(),
)
```
:::


Creating a store makes a request to Ollama to determine the embedding size. Ollama needs to be running and the model needs to be downloaded before you call `create()`.

## Choosing a model

Examples of embedding models available through Ollama include:

| Model                        | Dimensions |
| ---------------------------- | ---------- |
| `embeddinggemma-2` (default) | 768        |
| `nomic-embed-text`           | 768        |
| `mxbai-embed-large`          | 1024       |
| `all-minilm`                 | 384        |
| `bge-m3`                     | 1024       |

You can browse the full set on [Ollama's model search page](https://ollama.com/search?c=embedding). To see which models you've already pulled, run `ollama list`.

::: {.callout-note}
Use the same model for documents and queries in a store. To switch models, create a new store and embed your documents again.
:::

## Connecting to Ollama on another machine

If Ollama runs on a different machine or port, set `base_url=` to its address:

::: {#1fd7254b .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
provider = EmbeddingOllama(base_url="http://192.168.1.10:11434/v1")
```
:::


Include `/v1` in the URL to use Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API. By default, Ollama only accepts connections from the machine it's running on. To accept connections from other machines, configure `OLLAMA_HOST` on the server as described in [Ollama's FAQ](https://docs.ollama.com/faq).

The local Ollama server doesn't require an API key. If your server is behind a proxy that requires one, supply it with `api_key=`.

## Reconnecting to a store

`DuckDBStore.connect()` restores the provider's saved model name, server address, and batch size:

::: {#49c3024d .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.connect("my_store.db")
```
:::


Ollama needs to be running at the saved address, with the model available, when you add documents or search the store. A local Ollama server doesn't require an API key when reconnecting either.

::: {.callout-tip}
Use `EmbeddingOllama` when creating a store with Ollama. A store created with `EmbeddingOpenAI(base_url=...)` restores an OpenAI provider when you reconnect, which requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` to be set.
:::

## Troubleshooting

**Connection errors.** If you see an `APIConnectionError` (or a "connection refused" message), raghilda couldn't reach Ollama at the configured `base_url`. Check that the Ollama app is running, or start the server yourself with `ollama serve`. If Ollama is on another machine, double-check the address and port.

**Model not found.** An error like `model 'embeddinggemma-2:latest' not found` means Ollama is running but the model hasn't been pulled. Run `ollama pull embeddinggemma-2` (or whichever model you've configured) and try again.

For other errors, Ollama's [troubleshooting guide](https://docs.ollama.com/troubleshooting) explains where to find the server logs.

## Parameters

`EmbeddingOllama` accepts these optional parameters:

| Parameter    | Default                       | Description                                                                 |
| ------------ | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`      | `"embeddinggemma-2:latest"`   | Ollama embedding model name, as shown by `ollama list`                      |
| `base_url`   | `"http://localhost:11434/v1"` | Address of Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API                                   |
| `api_key`    | `None`                        | Only needed behind an authenticating proxy. A placeholder is used if `None` |
| `batch_size` | `20`                          | Texts per API call                                                          |

The store saves `model`, `base_url`, and `batch_size`. It doesn't save `api_key`. See the [`EmbeddingOllama` reference page](/reference/embedding.EmbeddingOllama.qmd) for API details.

## Complete example

This example builds a store from two web pages and searches it, using Ollama to embed the text locally. Replace the example URLs with pages you want to search:

::: {#90b22a96 .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingOllama
from raghilda.read import read_as_markdown
from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="docs.db",
    embed=EmbeddingOllama(model="embeddinggemma-2:latest"),
    name="docs",
    title="My Documentation",
    overwrite=True,
)

chunker = MarkdownChunker()
for url in ["https://example.com/doc1", "https://example.com/doc2"]:
    store.upsert(chunker.chunk(read_as_markdown(url)))

store.build_index()

chunks = store.retrieve("How do I configure authentication?", top_k=5)
for chunk in chunks:
    print(chunk.text[:200])
```
:::


You can also use `ChatOllama` in [chatlas](chatlas-integration.qmd) to run the chat model locally.

## Using Ollama with ChromaDB

When you pass `EmbeddingOllama` to `ChromaDBStore`, raghilda wraps it in an adapter so that ChromaDB can call it. The provider is restored automatically when you reconnect from Python, but ChromaDB clients in other languages won't be able to use the collection's embedding function. See [ChromaDB Embedding Functions](chromadb-embedding-functions.qmd) for details.

## Other local embedding options

[SentenceTransformers](embedding-sentence-transformers.qmd) also supports local embeddings. It loads the model inside your Python process. Ollama runs models in a separate server, which can accept requests from several applications.
